boundary-is-only-cue-context-flip: A faint border only needs strong contrast when it is the single hint a control exists, so the same grey border can fail on a borderless input yet pass elsewhere.
state-indicator-contrast-adjacent-surfac: The mark showing a control's state (a checkbox's tick, a toggle's thumb) must contrast 3:1 against the correct neighbouring surface, which is easy to pick wrong.
graphical-object-required-for-understand: Parts of a chart or diagram needed to understand it must contrast 3:1, but deciding which parts matter, and whether nearby text labels excuse them, needs a human.
f78-focus-indicator-occluded-but-present: A focus outline technically exists but is hidden by look-alike borders, so a keyboard user genuinely can't tell which control is currently focused.
adjacent-color-subsumption-and-compariso: Deciding which neighbouring colour to compare against is tricky: decorative borders and shadows should be ignored, and measuring the wrong pair gives the wrong pass/fail result.
focus-indicator-geometry-inner-border-pa: Where a focus indicator sits (inside, outside, or on the control's edge) decides which surface it must contrast against, so geometry, not one number, determines pass or fail.
exemption-boundaries-inactive-hover-esse: Several borderline cases (disabled controls, hover-only highlights, brand logos, symbolic glyphs like 'X' for close) need a human to decide whether the 3:1 contrast rule even applies.
